result:
Ticket 2 done. Summary of changes:

**`server/lib/server.ml`** — added `PUT/GET /blobs/**` handlers. `Server.router` now takes `data_dir`. Key segments are recovered via `Dream.target`/`Dream.split_target`/`Dream.from_path` rather than the deprecated `Dream.path` (confirmed deprecated even in the currently-released `dream.1.0.0~alpha8`). Nested directories are created with a small `mkdir_p`; PUT writes the raw body synchronously and returns `201` with a Yojson-encoded `{"key","sha256","size"}`; GET returns `200` with `application/octet-stream` or `404` if the file is missing.

**`server/bin/main.ml`** — passes `config.data_dir` into `Server.router`.

**`server/lib/dune`, `server/test/dune`, `Dockerfile`** — added `sha` (hashing) and `yojson` (JSON encoding) as explicit dependencies (both were already transitive deps of `dream`, now declared directly since we use them).

**`server/test/test_server.ml`** — added tests: PUT round-trip (status/JSON body), GET round-trip, nested-key subdirectory creation, GET-missing 404, and overwrite-on-existing-key.

One unrelated but blocking fix: the ticket-1 Dockerfile's `WORKDIR /build` created that directory as `root` (a known Docker quirk), so `dune build` failed with `mkdir(_build): Permission denied` under the non-root `opam` user — this wasn't triggered before since ticket 1 had no build-directory-writing step to expose it. Added `RUN sudo chown opam:opam /build` right after the `WORKDIR`.

Verified end-to-end: `docker build` runs `dune build` + `dune runtest` (all pass) in the image, and I ran the actual container via `run-server` and exercised it with real HTTP (curl from a container on the same compose network, since the sandbox can't reach the published port directly) — PUT/GET/overwrite/nested-key/404 all behaved per spec, sha256 matched `sha256sum`, and files landed on disk with subdirectories created as expected. Everything was torn down afterward (`docker compose down`, removed test image/containers).
